questions.prompt: A regional sales VP opens a discovery call by demanding "Build us a mobile CRM app by Q3." What is the Business Analyst's highest-leverage first question?

options.text: Which iOS SDK version do you prefer?
What underlying business problem or revenue bottleneck are we trying to solve, and how will we measure success?
How many buttons should be on the home screen?
Can we skip user interviews to save time?

questions.explanation: Strong BAs move stakeholders from premature solutions back to root business problems and measurable outcomes before scoping features.

rubric.label: Reframes solution requests into problem statements
Anchors discovery on measurable business outcomes

questions.prompt: Which elicitation technique is most effective for uncovering tacit operational steps and manual spreadsheet workarounds that staff forget to mention in interviews?

options.text: Emailing a 5-question yes/no survey
Job shadowing / direct observation in the live work environment
Reading a 3-year-old org chart
Reviewing server CPU graphs

questions.explanation: Observation / shadowing exposes real-world workarounds, exception paths, and friction points that verbal interviews frequently miss.

rubric.label: Matches elicitation technique to tacit knowledge

questions.prompt: During a cross-functional discovery workshop, Finance and Operations define "Active Customer" differently (billed in 90 days vs logged in within 30 days). What should the BA do?

options.text: Pick whichever definition is easier to query in SQL
Document both definitions in a shared Business Glossary, quantify the KPI variance, and facilitate executive alignment on a canonical definition
Use Finance's definition in odd months and Operations' in even months
Leave the definition ambiguous in the charter

questions.explanation: A shared Business Glossary eliminates conflicting dashboards and misaligned incentives across departments.

questions.prompt: Select ALL core components of a BABOK-aligned Current-State / Problem Analysis before proposing a solution.

options.text: Quantified pain points and baseline metrics
Root-cause analysis (e.g., 5 Whys or Fishbone diagram)
Impacted stakeholder groups and process bottlenecks
Final database indexing DDL script

questions.explanation: Discovery establishes quantified baselines, root causes, and stakeholder impacts before technical solution design begins.

rubric.label: Separates problem analysis from low-level implementation

questions.prompt: Why should a Business Analyst interview frontline operational staff in addition to senior sponsors during discovery?

options.text: Senior sponsors do not know the company name
Sponsors clarify strategic goals and budget, while frontline users reveal edge cases, compliance friction, and adoption barriers
Frontline staff approve capital budgets
To increase meeting count

questions.explanation: Combining executive intent with frontline operational reality prevents building solutions that fail adoption after launch.

rubric.label: Balances strategic intent with operational reality

questions.prompt: Customer support ticket volume rose 35% after a billing portal redesign, yet leadership assumes customers just need a FAQ PDF. Outline a concise 4-step discovery plan to validate the true root cause.
questions.explanation: Segment support tickets by reason code, analyze portal drop-off funnel analytics, run 5–8 contextual customer/agent interviews, and test root-cause hypotheses before prescribing a solution.

rubric.label: Combines quantitative ticket/funnel data with qualitative interviews
Validates hypotheses before jumping to solutions

questions.prompt: An automation initiative costs $120,000 upfront and saves $15,000 per month in operating expenses starting immediately after launch. What is the simple Payback Period?

options.text: 6 months
8 months
12 months
15 months

questions.explanation: Payback Period = Initial Investment / Monthly Net Savings = $120,000 / $15,000 = 8 months.

questions.prompt: Why is Net Present Value (NPV) preferred over simple undiscounted ROI when evaluating a 4-year enterprise transformation?

options.text: NPV ignores implementation costs
NPV accounts for the time value of money by discounting future cash flows back to today's value using the cost of capital
NPV always produces a higher number
Simple ROI cannot be expressed as a percentage

questions.explanation: Discounting multi-year cash flows reflects capital cost and risk; a positive NPV indicates value creation above the hurdle rate.

rubric.label: Applies time value of money via NPV
Distinguishes multi-year discounting from static ROI

questions.prompt: When comparing Build vs. Buy options in a Business Case, which cost category is MOST frequently underestimated in Total Cost of Ownership (TCO)?

options.text: Initial domain name registration
Ongoing maintenance, security patching, integration upkeep, and internal engineering opportunity cost over 3–5 years
One-time kickoff meeting snacks
Printing the project charter

questions.explanation: Custom software carries compounding 3–5 year maintenance and opportunity costs that must be weighed honestly against SaaS licensing.

questions.prompt: Select ALL essential sections of an executive-ready Business Case.

options.text: Strategic alignment and problem statement
Options analysis (including "Do Nothing" baseline)
Financial appraisal (costs, quantified benefits, payback/NPV, sensitivity assumptions)
Line-by-line CSS styling rules

questions.explanation: Decision-ready business cases compare realistic options against Do Nothing using transparent financial assumptions and sensitivity ranges.

rubric.label: Includes Do-Nothing baseline and options analysis
Grounds benefits in transparent financial assumptions

questions.prompt: A vendor claims their tool saves "10 hours per week across 50 analysts" ($50/hr = $130k/yr), yet no headcount is reduced and backlog revenue stays flat. How should a Senior BA classify this benefit?

options.text: Hard cash-flow cost reduction immediately bookable to P&L
Soft productivity / capacity-reallocation benefit unless tied to concrete avoided hiring or incremental revenue
Sunk cost
Capital expenditure

questions.explanation: Distinguishing hard P&L savings from soft capacity gains protects BA credibility with Finance and the CFO.

rubric.label: Separates hard P&L savings from soft capacity gains

questions.prompt: A VP proposes spending $250k on an AI chatbot to cut call-center volume by 20%. List the 4 key financial and risk assumptions you must stress-test in a sensitivity analysis before recommending approval.
questions.explanation: Stress-test true containment/deflection rate, cost per deflected call, customer adoption/escalation rate, and ongoing LLM/training/maintenance costs under conservative, base, and optimistic scenarios.

questions.prompt: Using the orders_ops dataset, calculate the Average Order Value (rounded to 2 decimals as avg_order_value) for PAID orders per customer region, ordered by avg_order_value descending.
questions.hint: JOIN customers c and orders o, filter WHERE o.status = 'PAID', GROUP BY c.region, and compute ROUND(AVG(o.total_amount), 2) AS avg_order_value.
questions.starterCode:
SELECT c.region, ROUND(AVG(o.total_amount), 2) AS avg_order_value
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE 
GROUP BY 
ORDER BY avg_order_value DESC;
questions.explanation: Computes regional Average Order Value (AOV) strictly over PAID orders so cancelled/refunded orders do not distort revenue KPIs.

questions.prompt: Segment the customer base in orders_ops by tier, returning tier and customer_count ordered by customer_count descending, then tier ascending.
questions.hint: SELECT tier, COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM customers GROUP BY tier ORDER BY customer_count DESC, tier ASC;
questions.starterCode:
SELECT tier, COUNT(*) AS customer_count
FROM customers
GROUP BY 
ORDER BY ;
questions.explanation: Provides an exact customer tier mix breakdown with deterministic tie-breaking by tier name.

questions.prompt: Quantify total non-PAID (at-risk or lost) order value in orders_ops as a single column named at_risk_revenue.
questions.hint: SELECT SUM(total_amount) AS at_risk_revenue FROM orders WHERE status != 'PAID';
questions.explanation: Sums CANCELLED ($900), PENDING ($1,500), and REFUNDED ($500) orders to highlight $2,900 in non-realized revenue.

questions.prompt: A support team is incentivized solely on minimizing Average Handle Time (AHT). Agents begin hanging up early or splitting single issues into 3 tickets. What phenomenon does this illustrate?

options.text: Goodhart's Law — when a measure becomes a target without guardrail metrics, it ceases to be a good measure
Pareto Optimality
Moore's Law
Statistical significance

questions.explanation: Always pair efficiency KPIs (AHT) with quality guardrails (First-Contact Resolution, CSAT, reopen rate) to prevent gaming.

rubric.label: Pairs primary KPIs with guardrail metrics

questions.prompt: What is the difference between a Leading Indicator and a Lagging Indicator in business performance tracking?

options.text: Lagging indicators measure past outcomes (e.g., quarterly churn); leading indicators predict future outcomes early enough to act (e.g., weekly feature adoption)
Leading indicators are always financial revenue totals
Lagging indicators cannot be charted
They are interchangeable

questions.explanation: Combining leading behavioral indicators with lagging financial outcomes allows teams to intervene before quarterly targets slip.

rubric.label: Connects leading signals to proactive action

questions.prompt: An A/B test on checkout pricing shows +4% conversion after only 12 hours and 80 visitors. Why should the BA advise against shipping immediately?

options.text: 12 hours is too long for an experiment
Stopping early ("peeking") on an underpowered sample inflates false-positive rates and misses day-of-week seasonality
Conversion rate should never increase
A/B tests only work on mobile apps

questions.explanation: Pre-committing to sample size, statistical power, and at least one full weekly cycle prevents shipping noisy false positives.

questions.prompt: In WSJF (Weighted Shortest Job First) prioritization, how is a backlog item's priority score calculated?

options.text: Cost of Delay divided by Job Size (Duration)
Job Size multiplied by Team Headcount
Lines of Code divided by Sprint Number
Budget minus Actual Cost

questions.explanation: WSJF = Cost of Delay / Job Size, maximizing economic value delivered per unit of scarce engineering capacity.

rubric.label: Optimizes economic value per unit effort

questions.prompt: In the Kano Model, how does a "Basic / Must-Be" attribute (such as accurate billing totals) behave regarding customer satisfaction?

options.text: Delivering it delights users exponentially
Its absence causes severe dissatisfaction, while delivering it merely prevents complaints rather than creating delight
Customers ignore it completely
It should always be deferred to Phase 3

questions.explanation: Must-Be hygiene expectations must be met reliably before investing heavily in Performance or Delighter features.

questions.prompt: What is the primary advantage of "vertical slicing" a user story over "horizontal slicing" (e.g., DB layer Sprint 1, API Sprint 2, UI Sprint 3)?

options.text: Horizontal slicing ships user value faster
Vertical slices deliver a thin, testable end-to-end increment of user value quickly, enabling early feedback and de-risking integration
Vertical slicing eliminates backend work
Horizontal slicing requires no QA

questions.explanation: Thin vertical slices validate assumptions with real users early and avoid late big-bang integration surprises.

rubric.label: Slices stories vertically for early feedback

questions.prompt: Select ALL elements of the RICE prioritization framework.

options.text: Reach (how many users/transactions impacted in a period)
Impact (magnitude of goal movement per user)
Confidence & Effort (certainty % divided by person-months)
Random alphabetical sorting

questions.explanation: RICE = (Reach × Impact × Confidence) / Effort, providing a transparent, comparable backlog ranking.

rubric.label: Balances impact against confidence and effort

questions.prompt: Two months after launching a new self-service onboarding flow, how should a Business Analyst conduct Benefits Realization?

options.text: Close the project because all Jira tickets are Done
Measure actual post-launch KPIs against the Business Case baseline, diagnose adoption gaps, and recommend follow-up optimizations
Delete the original Business Case
Only count how many commits were merged

questions.explanation: Output (shipped code) is not outcome (realized value); Benefits Realization closes the loop against the original business case.

questions.prompt: You have 1 sprint of capacity and three competing requests: (A) a regulatory compliance fix due in 14 days, (B) a high-reach checkout friction fix worth $40k/mo, and (C) an executive's cosmetic dashboard theme. Explain your prioritization and stakeholder communication plan.
questions.explanation: Prioritize (A) mandatory compliance deadline first, start thin vertical slice of (B) high Cost-of-Delay revenue fix with remaining capacity, and transparently defer (C) with economic rationale.

rubric.label: Ranks by regulatory risk and Cost of Delay
